about: The kernel's modules (E-004): one per concern, each with its purpose, what it takes and gives, what it may import and what it must not. test/ModulesTest.java holds every import in the source to this file. entryPoints are filled as each module is built. docs/MODULES.md is the readable form; it is written by hand until a generator exists (TODO.md 1.10) and says the same thing.
package: Each module's Java lives in its folder at the root under the package evaluator.<module> (evaluator.ingest, evaluator.score, ...); the module of an import is the segment after evaluator.
adding: To add a module: one entry here with every field; its folder appears with its first code. A module may import only what its mayImport lists; anything else is refused whether or not mustNotImport names it, so mustNotImport records the refusals worth saying. A new module or a new import is an architecture decision (theGhost.md E-004): draft the entry as a proposal, say you are waiting on Ghost, and stop; do not add it to main.

rules.rule: No module of the kernel imports a model client. Judgment lives in agent-runner/ (phase 2), behind a queue, and reaches the kernel only as facts.
rubric/ imports no module of ours: it is the vocabulary every other module speaks.
score/ reads rubric/ only and decides nothing about code: it combines facts the analyzers made. The referee does not read the players' code.
Nothing imports cli/: the command line names the work and does none of it.

rubric.purpose: The vocabulary: the seven metrics and their definitions as data, a Fact (what was measured, its evidence, its confidence, its state), the score card's types and invariants (docs/SCORE-CARD.md).

ingest.purpose: A repository on disk as an inventory: every source file by path and language, vendored and generated code set aside, nothing interpreted.
ingest.inputs: a path to a checked-out repository

analyze.purpose: Static analysis over the inventory, one adapter per language: complexity per function, the dependency graph, duplication, coupling, the test-to-code ratio, and the repo's own tests run in a sandbox.
analyze.outputs: the Complexity, Maintainability and tool-half-of-Quality facts

history.purpose: The git history's shape: spread over time, diff variance, reverts and fixups, tests landing beside code, agent fingerprints. Provenance layer 3.
history.inputs: a path to a checked-out repository with its .git

github.purpose: What GitHub verifies: commit signature status and push attribution for the account that submitted. Provenance layer 2. The only module that reaches the network, and only GitHub.
github.inputs: a repository name and the submitting account

score.purpose: Facts into a score card: the seven scores, the efficiency ratios, the provenance tier; the card as JSON and as Markdown. It reads no code and runs nothing.

cli.purpose: The command line: `evaluator score <path>` and nothing the other modules do not already do.
cli.outputs: the score card on stdout, what went wrong on stderr, an exit status
